post.description:
The v2 chat completions endpoint follows the OpenAI Chat Completions schema.

**API Key Usage**

- Authenticate with an API Key. When calling `chat/completions` with a personal key, passing `body.appId` in the request body is recommended.
- For OpenAI SDK compatibility, `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>-<appId>` is also supported without passing `body.appId`.
- Some SDKs append `/v1` to `baseURL` while others do not; if you receive a 404, try adjusting `/v1` in `baseURL`.
- `appId` resolution precedence: `body.appId` > `<apiKey>-<appId>` header suffix > legacy key-bound `appId`.

**Important Notes**

- Backend callers can pass `customUid` to identify their end users (passed to workflow `userId`). It does not change the authenticating member and is mutually exclusive with `authProxy` (max 1024 chars; empty string uses the default member; supported in FastGPT >= 4.18.0).
- To impersonate a team member via `authProxy`, a team owner must enable `authProxy` on the personal API key; the proxied member must still have access to the target app and chat session (FastGPT >= v4.15.0).
- Request fields such as `model` and `temperature` are ignored because model and inference parameters are controlled by the published app workflow.
- Standard `usage` tokens are placeholder values; set `detail=true` and sum `tokens` in `responseData` if you need per-node token usage.

**`chatId` Behavior**

- Omitted or empty: FastGPT server-side history is disabled; context is constructed solely from the request `messages` array.
- Non-empty string: FastGPT loads existing conversation history for `chatId` from storage and uses only the last message in `messages` as the user prompt (earlier entries are ignored). Ensure `chatId` is unique (max 1024 chars).

**`stream` / `detail` Combinations**

- `detail=false, stream=false`: Returns compact OpenAI-compatible JSON (`choices`, `usage`, `id`).
- `detail=false, stream=true`: Returns an OpenAI-compatible SSE stream with answer deltas and `[DONE]`.
- `detail=true, stream=false`: Includes `responseData` (per-node execution details) and `newVariables` in the JSON response.
- `detail=true, stream=true`: Returns a multi-event SSE stream (`answer`, `flowNodeStatus`, `flowNodeResponse`, `workflowDuration`, etc.).

Share-link calls use the same per-node SSE protocol with public fields filtered by share settings (`showCite`, `showRunningStatus`, `showSkillReferences`, and download permissions).

**Interactive Nodes**

If the workflow includes interactive nodes, set `detail=true`:

- `stream=true`: Read interactive payloads from `event: interactive`.
- `stream=false`: Read the `interactive` entry from `choices[].message.content`.

Non-streaming `interactive` payloads unwrap nested `children` / `loop` / `tool` wrappers down to the innermost prompt and strip internal runtime fields (`entryNodeIds`, `memoryEdges`, `nodeOutputs`). SSE frames may preserve wrapper envelopes whose inner payload sits under `params.childrenResponse`.

To resume execution after rendering the interactive prompt to the user, call this endpoint again with the same `chatId`:

- User selection: Send the selected option value directly as the user message `content`.
- Form input: Serialize the form key-value map as a JSON string in the user message `content`.

event_sandboxStatus.description: Shows visible sandbox lifecycle phases (`ready` allows tool execution, `failed` may carry `message`, skill deployment phases may include `skillName`). Phases represent distinct states rather than a fixed sequence.

event_error.description: Error emitted after the SSE stream opens, including plain `message` errors or structured business errors with `code`, `statusText`, and `data`. Do not rely on HTTP 200 alone.

409.description: Rejects the request when the conversation already has an active generation without persisting the rejected message. Non-streaming calls return HTTP 409; streaming calls emit the same payload on `event: error`. Use `data.responseChatItemId` to resume the active assistant message (or reuse the latest AI message when `data.reusePreviousAi=true`).

message.description: Localized display error message; use `code` or `statusText` for programmatic handling. Defaults to English when no translation is available.

responseChatItemId.description: Active assistant message ID currently generating on the server; clients should resume tracking this ID

reusePreviousAi.description: Indicates an interactive resume reusing the latest assistant message; refresh records before resuming

post.description:
Writes a stop flag for an active conversation and returns immediately. Clients should abort the open stream upon receiving success.
  The workflow halts scheduling at the next safe checkpoint; non-interruptible in-flight nodes such as HTTP requests still wait for their current step to finish.

post.description:
The v1 chat completions endpoint follows the OpenAI Chat Completions format. Standard OpenAI clients can point `baseURL` and `Authorization` to a FastGPT app.

**Important Notes**

- Backend callers can pass `customUid` to identify end users (forwarded to workflow `userId`). It does not change the authenticating member and is mutually exclusive with `authProxy` (max 1024 chars; empty string uses the default member; FastGPT >= 4.18.0).
- Request parameters such as `model` and `temperature` are ignored because model settings are defined by the published workflow.
- Standard `usage` tokens are placeholder values; set `detail=true` and sum `tokens` in `responseData` if needed.

**`chatId` Behavior**

- Omitted or empty: Server-side conversation memory is disabled; context comes solely from `messages`.
- Non-empty string: Loads existing conversation context for `chatId` and reads only the final entry of `messages` as the user prompt (earlier messages are ignored). Ensure `chatId` is unique (max 1024 chars).

**`stream` / `detail` Combinations**

- `detail=false, stream=false`: Returns compact OpenAI-compatible JSON (`choices`, `usage`, `id`).
- `detail=false, stream=true`: Returns an OpenAI-compatible SSE stream with answer deltas and `[DONE]`.
- `detail=true, stream=false`: Includes `responseData` and `newVariables` in the JSON payload.
- `detail=true, stream=true`: Returns a multi-event SSE stream (`answer`, `flowNodeStatus`, `flowResponses`, etc.).

**Interactive Nodes**

If the workflow includes interactive nodes, set `detail=true`:

- `stream=true`: Read interactive payloads from `event: interactive`.
- `stream=false`: Read the `interactive` entry inside `choices[].message.content`.

Non-streaming `interactive` payloads unwrap nested `children` / `loop` / `tool` wrappers down to the innermost prompt and strip internal runtime fields (`entryNodeIds`, `memoryEdges`, `nodeOutputs`). SSE frames may preserve wrapper envelopes whose inner payload sits under `params.childrenResponse`.

To resume execution after rendering the interactive UI, call this endpoint again with the same `chatId`:

- User selection: Pass the selected value directly as the user message `content`.
- Form input: Serialize the form object as a JSON string in the user message `content`.

Vector recall requires matching active embedding models across target datasets, and results respect collection-level permissions. Choose either `result.topk` (returns top 1–100 items without token truncation) or `result.maxTokens` (truncates on complete chunks with no fixed cap); defaults to `topk=20` when omitted, and prioritizes `topk` if both are sent. Response `meta` reports effective execution parameters.

ApiKeyAuth.description: Pass `Bearer <apiKey>` in the `Authorization` header. App API Keys automatically resolve their bound app so chat and companion endpoints omit `appId` (explicit `appId` or SDK suffixes cannot override key bindings). Personal keys must supply `appId` (via `body.appId` or `Bearer <apiKey>-<appId>` for OpenAI SDK compatibility; suffixes are never stored).
